sources.title: RFC 4987: TCP SYN Flooding Attacks and Common Mitigations

claims.text: RFC 9293 defines the three-way handshake and the LISTEN/SYN-SENT/SYN-RECEIVED/ESTABLISHED transitions. Each peer contributes a SYN carrying its initial sequence number and the peer acknowledges that SYN; SYN contributes one unit to segment sequence-space length, so the standard SYN/SYN-ACK/ACK example advances acknowledgment numbers by one.

RFC 9293 explicitly states that the principal reason for the three-way handshake is to prevent old duplicate connection initiations from causing confusion and provides an old-duplicate-SYN recovery example. The candidate correctly frames the third acknowledgment as completing confirmation of the responder's SYN rather than merely proving that both endpoints are online.

RFC 9293 keeps the passive opener in SYN-RECEIVED until an acceptable acknowledgment advances it to ESTABLISHED, and retransmission timeout processing retransmits the segment at the front of the retransmission queue. The candidate deliberately avoids asserting universal retry counts or timeout constants and only states that the synchronized peer continues to respond according to its current TCP state.

RFC 9293 describes normal close as independent termination of the two send directions: a TCP receiving FIN acknowledges it, can remain in CLOSE-WAIT until the local user closes, then sends its own FIN; the active closer commonly traverses FIN-WAIT-1/FIN-WAIT-2/TIME-WAIT while the passive closer traverses CLOSE-WAIT/LAST-ACK. Simultaneous close and acknowledgment aggregation mean four packets are common, not an invariant packet count.

RFC 4987 documents SYN flooding as exploiting state retention for half-open TCP connections after SYN receipt and explains that backlog, state allocation, reclamation, SYN cache and SYN cookie behavior are implementation-dependent. This supports the candidate's bounded statement that handshake state consumes resources while exact backlog and mitigation behavior must be verified for the target stack.

findings: Source-first review against RFC 9293 confirms the handshake state transitions, initial-sequence-number acknowledgment chain, old-duplicate-SYN rationale, normal and simultaneous close paths, FIN half-close semantics, and SYN/FIN sequence-space accounting used by the candidate.

The third-ACK-loss discussion is correctly bounded: the passive opener remains SYN-RECEIVED until an acceptable ACK, retransmission is governed by TCP retransmission processing, and the answer does not invent cross-platform retry counts or timers.

RFC 4987 independently supports the half-open-state resource/SYN-flood discussion and the candidate correctly keeps backlog, SYN-cookie and mitigation details behind an implementation-specific boundary.

All six assigned source-question variants are directly covered. The mechanism answer includes participants/state, entry-to-result flow, state transitions and guarantees, resource cost, implementation boundaries, failure paths, topic-specific follow-ups and a speakable short answer. No blocker, critical, major or actionable minor finding remains.
